subject: Air-gapped Handover playbook — redlines and inspection window
messages:
From: Amelia Trent <amelia.trent@isotech.com>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>
Cc: IsoTech Procurement <procure@isotech.com>, Dr. Javier Morales <j.morales@isotech.com>
Date: 2026-06-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Air-gapped deployment handover — initial info request

Hi Rohan,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. IsoTech is moving toward a private, air-gapped hosting model for the new imaging pipeline, and procurement asked me to collect the operational handover details we need to close the order form and MSA exhibits.

Specifically we need:
- A short runbook showing operator handover steps for an air-gapped environment (network isolation, media ingestion, operator access flow).
- Evidence options for operator access and attestation during an audit window (we typically allow a 2–4 hour inspection).
- Clarification on license scope in offline/on-prem scenarios (do model weights remain under Redwood license; what is allowed for snapshots/backup).

Can you send a draft playbook and indicate what evidence we can provide for audits? Procurement wants this by end of next week.

Best,
Amelia
Amelia Trent
Program Manager, Integrations
IsoTech Medical Systems
From: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>
To: Amelia Trent <amelia.trent@isotech.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-22T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Air-gapped deployment handover — initial info request

Hi Amelia — attaching a first-pass playbook (airgap-handover-v1.docx) and a short exhibit for operator runs (runbook-exhibitA.pdf). High level answers here:

1) Runbook: the attached covers handover steps, required on-site roles, media transfer steps (signed transfer manifest), and recommended offline validation checks.

2) Audit evidence: we can offer time-bound console snapshots, signed transfer manifests, an operator presence log, and a recorded verification checklist. For air-gapped installs where Redwood cannot reach the environment, we propose a joint inspection window (ISO-style) where an IsoTech auditor can review runbook execution and sample logs.

3) License scope: our standard on-prem exhibit covers model binary use by the customer subject to the MSA license terms; Redwood retains IP in model code and weights. We can add a clause that prevents redistribution of snapshots and requires destruction of intermediate transfer media after ingestion. Laura — I know you'll want to propose precise wording here.

I'll coordinate an internal redline and propose dates for a 3-hour inspection window the week of 6/29.

Thanks,
Rohan
Rohan Mehta
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
Attachments: airgap-handover-v1.docx; runbook-exhibitA.pdf
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-23T08:17:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Air-gapped deployment handover — initial info request

Rohan / team — quick redline and open questions (high level):

- License scope (MSA Exhibit A, section 2): propose language that affirms customer has a limited, non-transferable license to use the model weights for the single deployed environment and prohibits transfer of model weights offsite except as part of a documented, encrypted backup/restore process.

- Audit window: we should keep the audit window request narrow and controlled. Proposed approach: Redwood will provide a secured, timeboxed inspection consisting of (i) pre-signed console dumps for specified resource IDs, (ii) operator execution logs for the inspection period, and (iii) an on-site product SME who will not perform operator functions but will observe and attest to runbook fidelity. No persistent remote access.

- Evidence custody: if customer requires custody proof, propose mutual attestation form (signed by IsoTech and Redwood on completion) rather than escrow of keys or full-weight escrow — escrow triggers are high risk and involve legal/insurance elevation. If IsoTech insists on a custody arrangement, we should escalate to Legal / Finance for a commercial annex with indemnities and insurance.

- Operator credentials: do not include plaintext templates in the contract. Instead, reference a credentialing exhibit in which credential lifecycle (creation, rotation, destruction) is summarized and a sample template provided as an operational artifact (operator-credential-template.xlsx attached).

Open Qs for IsoTech: (1) will you accept mutual attestation instead of key escrow? (2) what are your required retention windows for inspection artifacts? (3) any regulator-driven constraints (HIPAA/HITRUST specifics) we should bake into exhibit?

Happy to take a redline pass on the MSA exhibit if you send a draft.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachments: operator-credential-template.xlsx
From: Amelia Trent <amelia.trent@isotech.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>
Cc: IsoTech Procurement <procure@isotech.com>, Dr. Javier Morales <j.morales@isotech.com>
Date: 2026-06-23T13:56:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Air-gapped deployment handover — initial info request

Thanks Laura — useful framing. Short answers to your open Qs:

1) Mutual attestation is acceptable to start; procurement may push for a short-term escrow-like proof-of-possession for the initial 90-day onboarding. We need Redwood's proposed attestation template to review.

2) Retention: our baseline is 12 months for inspection artifacts, but regulated installs may need 36 months; we'll flag the final requirement in the PO.

3) Regulator: this is a HIPAA-covered deployment — any PII/ePHI controls must appear explicitly; Dr. Morales is copied to confirm technical expectations.

Proposed inspection dates: June 30 or July 1 (US Pacific). Can Redwood confirm availability for a 3-hour window on either date?

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Amelia
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Amelia Trent <amelia.trent@isotech.com>, Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-24T16:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Air-gapped deployment handover — initial info request

Hi Amelia — Redwood ops can support either 6/30 or 7/1 for a 3-hour inspection; we propose the following plan:

- 30 min prep call (redwood SME + IsoTech auditor) to walk runbook steps.
- 2 hour joint inspection: sample console snapshots, transfer manifest review, and operator checklist execution with IsoTech observing.
- 30 min attestation and capture of signed checklist.

Action items:
- Amelia / IsoTech: confirm date and list of resource IDs you want included in pre-signed snapshots.
- Laura: I'll work with you to produce the mutual attestation template by EOD 6/25.
- Rohan / Aditya: please confirm the redline we should send procurement (we will not agree to persistent key escrow in the MSA without escalation).

We will send a short SOW addendum for the inspection effort and a proposed attestation form. If procurement needs a temporary custody check, we can offer a sealed-handover manifest process (technical, not key escrow) and record verification artifacts for retention.

Thanks — Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Director, Field Ops, Redwood Inference
